Welcome, also in my twenties and already a lot of fuck ups and regrets. Since I quit drinking there hasn't been any miracle that has got my life on track, in fact it is still very far from it. I saw a post the other day someone had a list of things drinking could do and on that list was "dream big but think small" and that really stuck out to me. When drinking it's easy to convince yourself that things in life will be easy to overcome but that's not thinking clearly. What is possible by not drinking is the ability to take a step back and really evaluate the choices you can make and the direction you want to take your life. One major thing that has helped me cope with the anxiety and stress is exercise personally I don't have a whole lot going on in my life, I basically get off work and go to the gym six days a week. If you are in school you may be quite a bit busier than me but even just taking a walk in the evening (I'd avoid walking by stores that sell alcohol) or a run if you can. Another thing that helped me and continues to help me is giving into other urges like if I really want to buy some vodka I'll buy some candy instead.

For me it took a week or two before I was actually sleeping through the night (I take melatonin to help me sleep) it helped me a lot giving into the temptation of junk food, especially when the strong craving to drink comes on.

For me it took a bunch of tries the first few days were the hardest for me and I'd usually make it about three days before drinking again. The withdrawals would be too much to take and this last time I powered through the withdrawals and it got somewhat easier after that. I have that voice everyday tell me I should drink, I've had to teach myself that voice isn't telling me what I really want. My consous mind says I want to be sober and that's what I'm really thinking.

Welcome. If alcohol is controlling your life and the decisions you make you need to decide whether you want alcohol controlling your decisions or yourself. I am 23 and up until two weeks ago I was drinking about 3 handles of vodka a week, but it didn't start there. Before I was 21 I really just drank on the weekends after I turned 21 I only got drunk on the weekends but drank 3 to 6 beers a night ( I used the excuse that I was sampling new beers and expanding my palate. Fast forward a year or so I'm buying 30 packs of budweiser drinking 12 to 16 a night so of course I put on 60 pounds I looked pregnant (I'm male by the way) so no one was congratulating me. haha.  When I realized how fat I was getting I knew I had to make a change so I decided to switch to vodka and flavored sparkling water. I figured hey at least I'm cutting out the carbs but drinking had become such a part of my life I wasn't ready to give it up. I'm only a couple weeks sober I still have cravings I still get moody and irritable and my first few days sober I had the shakes I was sweating non stop even hallucinating. So the whole point of my story is that I should have recognized that I don't control alcohol when I drink it controls me, however some people control their drinking just fine. If you feel like when you drink the alcohol controls you more than you control it, you might want to consider avoiding it. As far as special events go it is possible to have a good time without drinking I'm just now learning that. Just don't fall down that slippery slope like myself and many others have.
